question: Two parallel chords of a circle have lengths 10 cm and 4 cm, lie on the same side of the centre, and are 3 cm apart. Find the circle's diameter.
independent_reasoning: The perpendicular distances x,y from centre satisfy x²=r²−25, y²=r²−4 and y−x=3. Thus (y−x)(y+x)=21, so y+x=7, x=2,y=5; r²=29, diameter=2√29 cm.
source: Geometry 1.pdf, PDF page 5; exam/year not stated per item (PYQ status unverified)

question: Two triangles have AB=DB, AC=DC, and BC is common. Which congruence criterion proves △ABC≅△DBC?
independent_reasoning: The three corresponding sides are equal: AB=DB, AC=DC, and BC=BC; use SSS.

question: A circle has radius 5 cm. A chord is 6 cm long. Find its distance from the centre.
independent_reasoning: The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord; distance=√(5²−3²)=4 cm.
source: Geometry 4.pdf, PDF page 6; exam/year not stated per item (PYQ status unverified)

question: From an external point, two tangents are drawn to the same circle. One tangent segment is 12 cm. Find the other tangent segment.
independent_reasoning: Tangent segments from a common external point have equal lengths.
source: Geometry 4.pdf, PDF page 11; exam/year not stated per item (PYQ status unverified)

question: Two circles of radii 4 cm and 6 cm have centres 10 cm apart. Find the length of a direct common tangent segment.
independent_reasoning: For a direct common tangent, L²=d²−(R−r)²=100−4=96; L=4√6 cm.

question: At the intersection of two straight lines, one angle is 68°. Find the vertically opposite angle.
Two adjacent angles form a straight line. If one is 73°, find the other.
source: Geometry 2.pdf, PDF page 6; exam/year not stated per item (PYQ status unverified)

question: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. If an interior angle on one side is 118°, find the interior angle on the same side of the transversal at the other line.
independent_reasoning: Co-interior angles between parallel lines are supplementary: 180−118=62°.
source: Geometry 2.pdf, PDF page 7; exam/year not stated per item (PYQ status unverified)

question: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. An acute corresponding angle is 54°. Find the obtuse angle at the other intersection.
independent_reasoning: The matching acute angle is 54°; its adjacent linear-pair angle is 180−54=126°.
source: Geometry 2.pdf, PDF page 9; exam/year not stated per item (PYQ status unverified)

question: In a triangle, an exterior angle is 125° and one remote interior angle is 48°. Find the other remote interior angle.
The interior angles of a triangle include 47° and 68°. Find the third angle.
AB is parallel to CD. A zig-zag transversal makes angles 125° and 35° with the parallel directions at the two bends. Find the acute angle between its two segments.
independent_reasoning: The first segment's acute inclination is 180−125=55°; the second is 35° on the other side. Their included angle is 55+35=90°.
source: Geometry 2.pdf, PDF page 13; exam/year not stated per item (PYQ status unverified)

question: A cyclic quadrilateral has one interior angle of 112°. Find its opposite angle.
independent_reasoning: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary: 180−112=68°.
source: Geometry 3.pdf, PDF page 10; exam/year not stated per item (PYQ status unverified)

question: A chord of a circle is 10 cm long and is 12 cm from the centre. Find the circle's diameter.
independent_reasoning: The perpendicular bisects the chord; radius=√(12²+5²)=13 cm, so diameter=26 cm.
source: Geometry 5.pdf, PDF page 28; exam/year not stated per item (PYQ status unverified)

question: Two concentric circles have radii 5 cm and 3 cm. A chord of the larger circle is tangent to the smaller circle. Find the chord length.
independent_reasoning: The perpendicular from the common centre to the chord is 3 cm. Half-chord=√(5²−3²)=4 cm, so the chord is 8 cm.
source: Geometry 5.pdf, PDF page 29; exam/year not stated per item (PYQ status unverified)

question: A radius is drawn to the point where a tangent touches a circle. What is the angle between the radius and tangent?
independent_reasoning: The tangent at a point is perpendicular to the radius through that point.

question: From an external point P, PT is a tangent of length 12 cm, and a secant meets the circle at A then B. If PA=x cm and AB=7 cm, find x.
independent_reasoning: Tangent-secant theorem gives PT²=PA·PB, so 144=x(x+7). Thus x²+7x−144=0=(x−9)(x+16), and the positive length is 9 cm.
source: Geometry 5.pdf, PDF page 31; exam/year not stated per item (PYQ status unverified)

question: O is the circumcentre of △PQR. If ∠QOR=110° and ∠OPR=25°, find ∠PRQ.

question: In △ABC, D and E lie on AB and AC, respectively, and DE∥BC. If AD:DB=2:3, find AE:EC.
independent_reasoning: Thales/intercept theorem: parallel DE cuts the two sides proportionally, AD/DB=AE/EC=2/3.
source: Geometry 5.pdf, PDF page 15; exam/year not stated per item (PYQ status unverified)

question: The centroid G of a triangle divides median AD in the ratio AG:GD. Find this ratio.
independent_reasoning: The centroid lies two-thirds of the way from each vertex along a median, so AG:GD=2:1.
source: Geometry 5.pdf, PDF page 11; exam/year not stated per item (PYQ status unverified)

question: Two complementary angles are in the ratio 2:3. Find the smaller angle.
Two supplementary angles are equal. Find each angle.
independent_reasoning: Equal angles sum to 180°, so each is 90°.

question: A triangle has angles 90° and 35°. Find the third angle.
An isosceles triangle has vertex angle 40°. Find each base angle.
An equilateral triangle has side 9 cm. Find its perimeter.
In a triangle, the two opposite interior angles to an exterior angle are 52° and 61°. Find the exterior angle.
independent_reasoning: Exterior angle equals sum of remote interior angles=52+61=113°.

question: A triangle has side lengths 5 cm, 7 cm, and x cm. Which is the least possible integer x?
independent_reasoning: Triangle inequality requires x>|7−5|=2, so least integer x=3 (also x<12).

question: A right triangle has legs 6 cm and 8 cm. Find the hypotenuse.
A right triangle has hypotenuse 13 cm and one leg 5 cm. Find the other leg.
A linear pair has angle measures (3x+10)° and (2x+20)°. Find x.
Two vertically opposite angles measure (4x−5)° and (3x+15)°. Find x.
Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. A corresponding angle is 72°. Find its alternate interior angle.
independent_reasoning: Corresponding and alternate interior angles are equal for parallel lines.

question: The sum of interior angles of a quadrilateral is what?
independent_reasoning: A quadrilateral can be divided into two triangles; total=2×180=360°.

question: Find each interior angle of a regular hexagon.
Find the sum of the interior angles of a decagon.
Find each exterior angle of a regular 15-sided polygon.
A polygon has interior-angle sum 1260°. How many sides does it have?
A rectangle has length 12 cm and width 5 cm. Find its diagonal.
A square has diagonal 10√2 cm. Find its side.
independent_reasoning: For a square d=s√2; s=10 cm.

question: A rhombus has diagonals 10 cm and 24 cm. Find its side length.
A parallelogram has adjacent angles x° and (2x−30)°. Find x.
A rhombus has diagonals 16 cm and 30 cm. Find its area.
independent_reasoning: Area of a rhombus is half the product of its diagonals: (16×30)/2=240 cm².

question: In △ABC, AB=AC and ∠A=44°. Find each base angle.
The angles of a triangle are in ratio 2:3:4. Find the largest angle.
A right triangle has one acute angle 32°. Find the other acute angle.
independent_reasoning: Acute angles in a right triangle sum to 90°; 90−32=58°.

question: In △ABC, ∠A=50° and ∠B=70°. The bisectors of A and B meet at I. Find ∠AIB.
In △ABC, AD bisects ∠A. If AB=10, AC=15, and BD=8, find DC.
In △ABC, DE∥BC, with AD=6, DB=4, and AE=9. Find EC.
Triangles ABC and DEF are similar with side scale AB:DE=3:5. If area of ABC is 54 cm², find area DEF.
independent_reasoning: Areas scale as square of side ratio: 54×(5/3)²=150 cm².

question: Two similar triangles have corresponding sides 8 cm and 12 cm. If the smaller perimeter is 30 cm, find the larger perimeter.
independent_reasoning: Perimeters scale as corresponding sides: 30×12/8=45 cm.

question: A 1.5 m pole casts a 2 m shadow. At the same time, a tree casts a 12 m shadow. Find the tree's height.
independent_reasoning: Similar triangles: height/shadow=1.5/2; tree height=12×0.75=9 m.

question: A 10 m ladder reaches 8 m up a wall. How far is its foot from the wall?
The diagonal of a rectangle is 25 cm and one side is 7 cm. Find the other side.
A square's side is increased from 8 cm to 12 cm. By how much does the square of its diagonal increase?
independent_reasoning: For side s, diagonal squared is 2s²; change=2(12²−8²)=160 cm².

question: A parallelogram has one angle 118°. Find its adjacent angle.
independent_reasoning: Adjacent angles in a parallelogram are supplementary; 180−118=62°.

question: A rhombus has one interior angle 64°. Find its smallest angle.
independent_reasoning: Opposite angles equal 64°; adjacent angles are 116°, so smallest=64°.

question: A quadrilateral has angles 75°, 92°, and 108°. Find its fourth angle.
A regular polygon has exterior angle 30°. Find its number of sides.
A regular octagon has how many diagonals?
A regular pentagon has interior angle sum what?
A cyclic quadrilateral has opposite angles (3x+10)° and (5x−6)°. Find x.
In △ABC, AB=AC and ∠A=36°. The bisector of ∠B meets AC at D. Find ∠BDC.
independent_reasoning: Base angles B=C=72°. In △BCD, ∠CBD=36° and ∠BCD=72°, so ∠BDC=180−36−72=72°.

question: In △ABC, AD is an angle bisector, AB=12 cm, AC=18 cm, BC=20 cm. Find BD.
A line parallel to one side of a triangle cuts the other two sides in ratios 3:2 from the corresponding vertices. If the smaller triangle area is 81 cm², find the whole triangle area.
independent_reasoning: Side scale small:whole=3:(3+2)=3/5; area scale=9/25; whole=81×25/9=225 cm².

question: Two similar triangles have area ratio 25:49. A corresponding side of the smaller triangle is 15 cm. Find the corresponding side of the larger triangle.
A right triangle has altitude from the right angle to its hypotenuse, splitting the hypotenuse into 9 cm and 16 cm segments. Find the altitude.
independent_reasoning: Altitude is geometric mean: h²=9×16, so h=12 cm.

question: In a right triangle, the hypotenuse is 25 cm and one leg is 15 cm. Find the radius of its incircle.
independent_reasoning: Other leg=20; for right triangle r=(a+b−c)/2=(15+20−25)/2=5 cm.

question: The sides of a triangle are 13 cm, 14 cm, and 15 cm. Find its inradius.
A triangle has sides 10 cm, 17 cm, and 21 cm. Find the length of the median to the 21 cm side.
In triangle ABC, AB=10 cm, AC=14 cm, and BC=16 cm. Find the length of the angle bisector from A.
In an isosceles triangle with equal sides 13 cm and base 10 cm, find the radius of the incircle.
A regular polygon has each interior angle 165°. Find the number of sides.
The interior-angle sum of a polygon is four times its exterior-angle sum. How many sides does it have?
A convex polygon has 54 diagonals. Find its number of sides.
In a cyclic quadrilateral, one angle is twice its opposite angle. Find the larger of the two opposite angles.
independent_reasoning: Let angles x and 2x. x+2x=180 ⇒ larger=120°.

question: A cyclic quadrilateral has consecutive angles (2x+10)°, (3x−5)°, and (x+20)°. Find the fourth angle.
independent_reasoning: Opposite first and third sum 180: (2x+10)+(x+20)=180 ⇒x=50. The second angle is 145°; its opposite is 35°.

question: Two chords AB and CD intersect at P inside a circle. If AP=4, PB=9, CP=6, find PD.
From point P, a tangent PT and a secant PAB are drawn. If PA=5 cm and AB=7 cm, find PT.
A chord of a circle of radius 17 cm is 8 cm from the centre. Find the chord length.
Two parallel chords of lengths 16 cm and 30 cm lie on opposite sides of a circle's centre. Their distances from the centre are 15 cm and 8 cm. Find the circle's radius.
independent_reasoning: For chord 16, half=8 and distance=15; r²=8²+15²=289, so r=17 cm. For chord30 half=15, d=8 also gives17.

question: A circle has radius 10 cm. A chord subtends a central angle of 120°. Find the chord length.
An inscribed angle intercepts a major arc of 250°. Find the measure of that inscribed angle.
independent_reasoning: An inscribed angle equals half its intercepted arc: 250/2=125°.

question: Two tangents from P touch a circle at A and B. If ∠AOB=136°, find ∠APB.
independent_reasoning: OA⊥PA and OB⊥PB; quadrilateral OAPB has two right angles, so ∠APB=180−136=44°.

question: A circle is inscribed in a triangle with side lengths 13, 14, and 15 cm. Find the total length of the three tangent segments from each vertex to its two contact points.
independent_reasoning: At each vertex the two tangent segments are equal; their combined total across vertices equals the triangle perimeter 42 cm.

question: A triangle has sides 7 cm, 15 cm, and 20 cm. Find the radius of its circumcircle.
In △ABC, medians AD and BE meet at G. If area △ABC is 90 cm², find area △ABG.
independent_reasoning: The centroid partitions the triangle into six equal-area small triangles; ABG comprises two, so area=90/3=30 cm².

question: In triangle ABC, D is midpoint of BC. If AB²+AC²=250 cm² and BC=10 cm, find AD.
A triangle has sides 5 cm, 12 cm, and 13 cm. Find the distance from the right-angle vertex to the midpoint of the hypotenuse.
independent_reasoning: In a right triangle, median to hypotenuse equals half the hypotenuse, 13/2=6.5 cm.

question: The sides of a triangle are 9 cm, 10 cm, and 17 cm. Find the median to the side of length 17 cm.
